maria.t: Quick follow-up after the RFC review: proposing a small policy gateway that evaluates rollout rules outside of the router process. Keeps routing fast.
ben.w: sounds good. gateway = policy-as-a-service? what does the contract look like?
lee: yes. simple sync RPC: input = route_id, request_meta, recent_signals; output = decision blob with ttl and confidence. router caches decisions.
sre_ryan: what signals are in 'recent_signals'? latency histograms? sample errors? golden eval diffs?
maria.t: start minimal: p95/p99 latency, error_rate, anomaly_flag, eval_regressions_score. enrich with request risk_tier and region.
ben.w: we also need circuit-breaker heuristics: backoff multiplier, cooldown window, and max-diversion-percent. add to decision blob.
lee: draft response prototype: ```{action:DIVERT, target:stable-v1, diversion_pct:100, cooldown_s:900, backoff:2.0, ttl_s:60, code:LATENCY_P99}```
sre_ryan: please use enumerated codes (LATENCY_P99, OOM, EVAL_REGRESSION) not free text. ops tooling depends on those.
ben.w: runbook-wise, SREs need a one-click escape that sets decisions to DIVERT->stable globally. also requires audit trail and reason.
maria.t: agreed. escape API must be an authenticated endpoint that writes a high-priority decision into the KV with a source_tag and expiration.
lee: KV placement: prefer region-local KV with optional global override. that avoids cross-region latency for normal operations. global writes for org-incidents.
sre_ryan: TTLs are tricky. short TTLs cause flapping; long TTLs delay recovery. propose exponential cooldown: initial 60s, double on repeat until cap 1h.
maria.t: good pattern. also add 'stability_window' signal: require X successful minutes before removing diversion.
ben.w: observability: decision traces must travel with request_ids. store policy inputs (signal snapshot) and outputs for 7 days. searchable for postmortems.
lee: cost control: policy gateway should be able to declare a cost-action LOW_COST_FALLBACK that picks quantized or smaller-context variants. router implements the mapping.
sre_ryan: hedging tradeoff: we don't want automatic hedging on every route. make hedging opt-in per route with budget tokens per minute.
maria.t: and label requests with risk_tier:LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH so policy can choose aggressive fallback only for LOW.
ben.w: developer ergonomics: policy-as-code DSL in repo. changes go through CI which runs a policy simulator on synthetic traffic and historical signals. fail-fast if the policy would have diverted incorrectly historically.
lee: implement a lightweight expression language: rules combine signals and thresholds, allow weighted scoring. keep it intentionally small.
sre_ryan: for Dedicated/Private customers we should provide a local policy runtime binary + a shim that reads the central policy repo. so they can run without the hosted gateway.
maria.t: yes, tiny surface: eval_ruleset (read-only), decision_endpoint (optional local), and a sync worker for policies.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: policy-gateway v0.2 staged by @maria.t at 5301112240 :rocket:
ben.w: action items: 1) lee to draft decision blob schema and KV semantics, 2) maria to write policy DSL primer + enumerated codes, 3) ryan to design escape API and cooldown strategy.
lee: I'll include sample circuits and backoff default values.
maria.t: I'll add the simulation checklist for CI.
sre_ryan: we should sync with product on user-visible degradation messaging (graceful degrade vs hard rollback).
maria.t: noted. let's reconvene Thu. short thread but covers the gaps I wanted. thanks all.
